title: What If It Barely Rained for 22 Years? The Southwest Lived It

scenes.text: What if it barely rained for 22 years? The American Southwest just lived through it.
From 2000 to 2021, rain and snow ran about 8 percent below normal, and temperatures ran nearly one degree Celsius hotter.
Tree rings show it was the driest 22-year stretch in at least 1,200 years, worse than the megadrought of the late 1500s.
In 2021, Lake Mead and Lake Powell both hit record lows, and Mead got its first federal water shortage declaration.
scenes.keywords: lake mead low water bathtub ring

scenes.text: Scientists attribute about 19 percent of that drought's severity to human-caused climate trends.
Without that warming, it probably wouldn't count as a megadrought. One study put the odds of another dry year at about 94 percent.
